notes: Hermes variant: `hermes chat` runs one turn, is exited cleanly (Ctrl-D → process_exited), then relaunched as `hermes chat -r <id>`. Hermes has NO transcript file — continuity is the shared SQLite store, and resume REUSES the same sessions row: _preload_resumed_session keeps session_id as the target and clears ended_at/end_reason, while the sessions upsert never rewrites started_at. So ONE store session id spans TWO PID lifetimes. Hermes is a presession adapter: the daemon first sees a proc-<PID> row (Hermes INSERTs the sessions row only on the first user message, ~2s in), which then hands off to the real store id — so the birth is modelled as TWO phases and every later phase pins to session_birth via same_session_as, never to the presession row (which never goes working). The reopen itself emits NO event (reconcile returns early when neither message_count grew nor the session just ended), so the second lifetime's first observable is transcript_activity from the resumed turn — that is what v2_resume_rebind asserts. observations: model is left unpinned (it comes from the recording home's config.yaml) and cost_nonzero is not asserted (Hermes reports 0.0 under billing_mode='subscription_included' and the adapter re-prices from irrlicht's alias table); record fills both.

text: First launch: the hermes process is scanned and a proc-<PID> presession appears in ready, before Hermes has written any sessions row
Hermes INSERTs the sessions row on the first user message; the watcher discovers it and the real store session id is born in ready — a DIFFERENT session_id than the presession
First user prompt drives the store session ready → working
finish_reason='stop' on the newest assistant row settles the first turn back to ready
Clean exit (Ctrl-D, performed by the resume step) after turn 1: process_exited on the store session
Spec: 'Same session_id reappears (not a new session row)' — after `hermes chat -r <id>`, activity resumes on the SAME store session id under a new PID; no second session row is created
Spec: 'ready → working on the first new turn' — the second lifetime's prompt drives the SAME session to working
Second turn completes back to ready on the SAME session — each PID lifetime's arc is independently correct, and the run ends in ready
